snippet.title: EMP Charges 🗿 Kortz Center Heist Prep • GTA 5 Online
snippet.description:
EMP Charges is a Optional prep mission featured in Grand Theft Auto Online as part of the The Kortz Center Heist update. It is a freeroam mission to help progress The Kortz Center Heist. The objective is to obtain EMP charges to overload the electricity of the Kortz Center's Bell Building and cause a temporary blackout during the heist finale. This optional prep work is only available if the player has scoped the Electrical Box in the exterior of the Bell Building during Scope Out Kortz Center. Raf gives a brief background information about now financially-broken Merryweather Security, trying to restore their reputation by looking hirable with their recently acquired equipment, which is currently being hauled in the back of an armored Hauler Custom truck. Raf sends the location of the Merryweather's armored truck. The player is instructed to force the armored truck to stop, so they can enter around the back of the Mobile Operations Center trailer. Inside it, the player must search for the EMP charges, steal the Rumpo Custom inside it, leave the Mobile Operations Center and park the vehicle at the Kortz Center to complete the optional prep work. 

“So, everyone knows Merryweather's trying to save their rep in LS. I heard they're hauling new equipment, trying to look tough, hirable y'know? There's gotta be some EMPs in this convoy, the kinda charges we need to throw the Kortz Center into darkness. So I'm thinking, stop the truck, steal the charges, humble Merryweather.”

Mission Details: Steal a device that can trigger an electro-magnatic pulse to disable the lights and some keypads inside the Kortz Center.

Heist Impact: Disabled the lights inside the Kortz Center and unlocks access to an additional staircase into the basement

The Kortz Center Heist update adds a new Heist and players can purchase an Art Studio for their owned Mansions via the Prix Luxury Real Estate website, gaining access to the new Heist. This Heist contains a range of Prep Missions leading to a Finale, where players steal works of art from the Kortz Center that can be sold for profit or displayed in their owned Mansions. Players can launch Prep Missions from the Planning Board located inside the Art Studio, or by calling Raf De Angelis via the phone menu in Freemode. This Heist can be completed by 1–4 players.

Stop the armored truck. Enter the armored truck. Locate the EMP charges. Steal the EMP charges. Enter the Rumpo Custom. Exit the armored truck. Park the Rumpo Custom at the Kortz Center. Arm the EMP charge. Leave the area. EMP charge armed.

snippet.title: The Hidden Kitchen That Keeps You Alive When The Grid Goes Down
snippet.description:
Your house has a second kitchen. It only appears when the grid dies — and most people never find it.

When the power goes out, the real danger isn't hunger. In the February 2021 Texas blackout (Winter Storm Uri), 4.5 million homes and businesses went dark, 14.6 million people fell under boil water notices, and more than 1,400 Texans were poisoned by carbon monoxide — most of them following the one safety rule everyone already knows. When the state counted the 246 dead, starvation wasn't on the list. Hypothermia was the leading cause. A hot meal is the only heater that works from the inside out.

This file covers the complete second kitchen hiding in your house right now: why your gas oven dies with the grid and which burners don't, the water heater trick that serves a warm first course ten minutes into a blackout, the freezer decision that turns a dying asset into allies, the four carbon monoxide rules nobody teaches, the real fuel math on a 20 lb propane tank (430,000 BTU), the hundred-year-old haybox method that cooks dinner on five minutes of flame, the one-dollar military flameless ration heater (the MRE heater) that works in a sealed room, and why half the freeze-dried survival pantry is writing checks your water can't cash.

No grid. No panic. Under $100 — and most of it is hardware you already own.

This video is for educational purposes. Follow manufacturer safety instructions for all fuel-burning appliances, keep generators at least 20 feet from any opening, and run a battery-powered carbon monoxide alarm.

snippet.title: UK Government emergency plan: should we be stockpiling?
snippet.description:
Why is everyone talking about stockpiling?

The UK government has confirmed to Channel 4 News that it is now set to launch a new plan to prepare ready for emergencies.

Extreme weather, cyber attacks and AI interference are just some of the dangers the government has said we should get ready for.
But, as the wait goes on for official guidance to be published. Some content creators have filled that void.

In this episode of the breakdown we look at why the government is talking about being prepared now, what being prepared actually looks like, and how worried we should actually be.
We also speak to Professor Hannah Cloke, an expert on risk and resilience from the University of Reading.

The government told the breakdown in a statement that it will launch a public awareness campaign - and that these were “normal practice across Europe”.
A spokesperson added: Following a difficult summer, the Prime Minister has been clear that Britain must become more resilient and better prepared for the challenges we face.”

snippet.title: Europe’s Meltdown, Scorching Heat, Failing Grids Blackouts Loom Across EU| Times Now World
snippet.description:
Europe is facing a summer of energy chaos as record-breaking heatwaves expose the fragility of its power grids. With temperatures soaring above 40°C in countries like France, Croatia, and Hungary, electricity demand has surged as millions turn to air conditioning. Spain saw a 14% jump in consumption during July’s heatwave, while France and Germany also reported dangerous demand spikes. Yet, as demand rises, supply is collapsing. France’s nuclear plants have been forced to cut output due to overheated rivers, while Italy’s ageing infrastructure triggered blackouts across cities like Rome and Milan. Renewables provided mixed relief: solar hit record highs in June, but stagnant winds left turbines across the UK and Finland nearly idle, forcing a return to gas. Experts warn that Europe’s power systems — built for milder climates — are unprepared for extreme weather, making each summer heatwave a potential trigger for continent-wide blackouts. Without urgent investment in resilient grids, flexible storage, and cleaner energy, Europe risks spiraling deeper into an energy crisis.

snippet.title: 72 Hours No Help! The Lightweight Kid’s Survival Kit
snippet.description:
72 Hours No Help! The Lightweight Kid’s Survival Kit  Teaching My Son Survival: Knife Sharpening, Water Safety, and a 72-Hour Kids Survival Pack. In this video, I teach my son how to prepare for the unexpected by building his own 72-hour kids survival pack — complete with shelter, food, fire, water, and essential tools. We start with one of the most important skills: how to sharpen his everyday carry knife using a diamond sharpener. I explain why a bright orange safety vest can make the difference between being lost and being found, and I test his knowledge with real-world questions like, “What should you do if you need clean water?” (Spoiler: he knows to boil it!)

Many of you ask how to make a survival kit for kids. We go deeper into water purification, covering why boiling isn’t enough to remove chemicals and how chlorine tablets add a crucial layer of safety. This video is more than just gear — it’s about building confidence, problem-solving skills, and real-world readiness in the next generation.

Whether you’re putting together a kids 72-hour survival kit, a family bug-out bag, or simply teaching your children how to think and act in a crisis, this step-by-step breakdown is the perfect place to start.

snippet.title: Urgent! Every INDIAN Write Down! SINGLE 112 Phone Emergency Number in India #shorts
snippet.description:
The Supreme Court's recent direction to make 112 the single national emergency number across India may seem like a simple administrative change, but its impact on ordinary citizens could be significant. For decades, Indians have had to remember different emergency numbers for police, ambulance, fire services, women's safety, child protection, and other emergencies. In moments of panic, confusion about which number to call can waste valuable time. The Court has emphasized that emergency response should be simple, accessible, and effective, especially when a person's life may be at risk.

The idea behind a unified emergency number is straightforward: one number should connect citizens to all critical emergency services. Whether someone is facing a road accident, a medical emergency, a fire, a crime, or a threat to personal safety, dialing 112 should trigger a coordinated response. Instead of citizens having to determine which department to contact, the emergency response system itself can identify the situation and dispatch the appropriate services. This approach places the burden of coordination on the government system rather than on the person in distress.

One of the biggest advantages of the reform is speed. In emergencies, even a delay of a few minutes can have serious consequences. A heart attack patient waiting for an ambulance, a victim of a road accident needing trauma care, or a family trapped in a fire cannot afford confusion over multiple helpline numbers. A single national number reduces decision-making time and allows emergency operators to quickly connect the caller with the required assistance. The Supreme Court has linked this issue to the constitutional right to life, recognizing that access to timely emergency services is an essential part of protecting citizens.

The reform could be especially beneficial for rural populations, migrant workers, elderly citizens, children, and tourists. Many people may not know the different emergency numbers or may struggle to remember them during stressful situations. A nationwide "one nation, one emergency number" system is easier to learn and communicate. Schools, public campaigns, and community programs can focus on teaching just one number, increasing public awareness and improving emergency preparedness across the country.

Another important aspect is the integration of technology and emergency management. A centralized 112 system can allow police, ambulance, and fire departments to coordinate more effectively. Modern emergency response centers can use location tracking, computer-aided dispatch systems, and real-time communication to reduce response times. Instead of separate agencies operating in isolation, the system can function as a single network focused on helping citizens as quickly as possible.

The move also brings India closer to international best practices. Many countries operate with a single emergency number, such as 911 in the United States and 112 across much of Europe. These systems are designed to be simple, memorable, and universally recognized. By strengthening the 112 Emergency Response Support System, India is moving toward a model that prioritizes ease of access and rapid response, which are essential features of a modern public safety infrastructure.

If implemented effectively by states and local authorities, the Supreme Court's direction could become one of the most practical governance reforms in recent years. Citizens may not notice its importance in everyday life, but during an emergency it could mean the difference between confusion and immediate help, between delayed assistance and a timely response, and in some cases, between life and death. The success of the reform will ultimately depend on how well emergency services are integrated, staffed, and equipped, but the vision of a single emergency number represents a major step toward a more citizen-friendly and responsive system.

snippet.title: 5 EMP Myths Even Preppers Still Believe
snippet.description:
Think an EMP means every car dies, the grid is gone forever, and a single gap ruins your Faraday cage? Hollywood and a lot of prepper content get these wrong. In this video I go through five common EMP myths, what the research says, and how the real picture should change where you put your prep effort. I added some sources below.

0:00 – Hollywood EMP vs. reality

3:45 – Myth 4: We'd be set back to the 1800s forever
4:45 – Myth 5: A Faraday cage has to be perfect
5:40 – The takeaway

The reality sits between "instant apocalypse" and "nothing to worry about," and that middle ground tells you where to spend your time and money.

snippet.title: Could the UK Electricity Grid Fail?
snippet.description:
Is the UK electricity grid at risk of blackouts? We look at the alarming events of 23 June and ask if our power network is truly fit for purpose.

In Part 1 of our summer energy mini-series on The Business, Dominic O’Connell examines the growing strain on the UK electricity grid as Britain races towards its legally binding net zero commitments. From surging constraint costs to unmetered solar generation, we break down why modernising electricity transmission is vital for the wider UK economy and long-term economic growth.

We are joined by Adam Bell, former head of energy strategy for the government and partner at StoneHaven, to explore how shifting to renewables creates unprecedented stability challenges. Plus, energy developer and data analyst Ben Watts (creator of Kilowatts Grid) shares his startling analysis of what went wrong on the UK electricity grid on 23 June, and why calls are growing for greater regulation of NESO (National Energy System Operator). Can politicians protect British business and consumers from soaring power bills while overhauling energy fiscal policy?

snippet.title: Something BIG Is Happening Beneath America — Earthquakes Are Piling Up
snippet.description:
Something BIG is happening beneath America. In just a few days, earthquakes hit off Vancouver Island, near Petrolia in northern California, around Puget Sound and Seattle, in Nevada, and near Los Angeles. At the same time, a solar storm is heading for Earth and Hurricane Polo has hit Baja California. Are these earthquakes connected, or is it just a coincidence?

In this video, we break down the Cascadia subduction zone, the Juan de Fuca plate, and the San Andreas fault in simple words. You will learn how sea floor mud cores point to a link between Cascadia and the San Andreas, what the Puget Sound earthquake pattern says about the next big quake, and whether solar storms and coronal holes can really affect earthquakes. We separate what is proven from what is only a theory.

You will also get simple earthquake preparedness tips from a former firefighter and hazmat technician, including what to do during shaking, what to keep in your emergency kit, and how to stay safe in a tsunami zone.
